AI-Assisted Data Science Elective Recommender:
Connecting Course Choices, Skills, and Career Pathways
Student Researcher
Ashutosh Modi
Faculty Mentor
Marco Scipioni
Academic Unit
School of Data Science, UNC Charlotte
Project Period
Fall 2026 – Spring 2027
1. Problem and Significance
Choosing electives can be difficult for Data Science students. Students may rely on word of mouth
or select courses without fully understanding what skills they will gain or how those courses
connect to future careers. Large language models can make this information easier to explore
through a conversational interface. This project will develop an AI tool to help students make more
informed elective choices by connecting courses to skills and career paths. The goal is to support,
not replace, academic advisors.
2. Student-Originated Research Question and Objectives
The project’s main research question is:
Can an AI tool help Data Science students choose electives that better match their interests and
career goals?
The project will build an LLM-based interface for students, connect electives to skills and careers,
test the system with realistic student questions and career profiles, and measure how accurate and
useful the recommendations are.
3. Background and Approach
The system will use official UNC Charlotte course information together with a large language
model. Students will be able to enter their interests or career goals and receive elective

recommendations.

Course Syllabus
DTSC 2301 Modeling and Society
 

Course Description
In this studio, students learn how to use statistical methods/tools and query languages on relational databases to explore a data science approach to socially relevant challenges associated with a social science discipline. Ethical implications of collecting and using data from external sources are also discussed.

Prerequisites: DTSC 1302 and STAT 1220 or STAT 1221 or STAT 1222
Student Learning Outcomes

Technical Proficiency in Data Science
	•	Master Git for version control and collaborative workflows.
	•	Build skills in exploratory data analysis (visualizations and statistical
	•	techniques).
	•	Gain an understanding of regression techniques and model performance
	•	metrics.
	•	Learn to detect, handle, and impute missing data.
	•	Identify and mitigate bias and overfitting in models.

Ethical Implications and Challenges in the Practice of Data Science and Data Analysis
	•	Evaluate ethical frameworks in the context of data science.
	•	Analyze case studies on ethical data usage, data ownership, and the societal impact of AI.
	•	Understand the environmental, social, and ethical considerations in predictive analytics and data science.

Critical Thinking in Data Analysis
	•	Formulate effective research questions.
	•	Develop professionalization skills.

techniques and work with a variety of professionals, from artists to
writers, to being the vision for an interactive game or media product to
life. The certificate may be pursued concurrently with any of the
undergraduate degree programs at UNC Charlotte.

Casino Crime Data Analysis
Total Points: 40
Use the Casino dataset (CASINO.Rdata) containing the number of employees and crime rate for 10
observations to answer the following questions in R.

2 18 1.63
3 24 2.33
4 22 2.41

Question 1: Least Squares Regression Line (8 points)
Fit a simple linear regression model with CRIMERATE as the response variable and EMPLOYEES as
the predictor variable.
a) Write the equation of the fitted least squares regression line in the form: ■ = β■0 + β■1x
b) Interpret the meaning of β■0 and β■1 in the context of this problem.
Question 2: Coefficient of Determination (6 points)
a) Extract and report the coefficient of determination (R²) from your model.
b) Interpret the R² value in the context of this problem. What percentage of variation in crime rate is
explained by the number of employees?
c) Based on the R² value, would you say this is a good fitting model? Explain briefly.
Question 3: Confidence Intervals for Regression Coefficients (8 points)
a) Construct 95% confidence intervals for both β0 and β1.
b) Interpret the 95% confidence interval for β1 (the slope) in context.

c) Does the confidence interval for β1 include zero? What does this suggest about the relationship
between employees and crime rate?

Syllabus for STAT 3160-02: Applied Multivariate Analysis
Fall 2026

Course Description
This course introduces applied multivariate analysis methods for exploring and understanding complex multivariate data encountered in real-world applications. The course begins with developing intuition for multivariate data through exploratory data analysis and simple statistical methods using practical examples. Building on this foundation, students will learn major multivariate techniques, including factor analysis, correspondence analysis, cluster analysis, and multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA). Each method will be motivated by real-world applications, explained through examples, and reinforced through homework assignments and hands-on data analysis activities. Emphasis will be placed on understanding the structure of multivariate data, selecting appropriate analytical methods for different research questions and data types, and interpreting and communicating analytical results in meaningful contexts. Students will gain practical experience analyzing multivariate datasets and presenting statistical findings using R or Python.
Textbook
No textbook purchase is required for this course. All required readings and course materials will be provided in PDF format through Canvas in advance.
